record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist an oracle D relative to which catalytic logspace becomes as powerful as EXP; that is, can one show CL^D = EXP^D?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Show the existence of an oracle D such that CLD = EXPD.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Catalytic logspace, denoted CL, is the class of languages decidable by a Turing machine equipped with a read-only input tape, an O(log n)-size read/write work tape, and an additional 2^{O(log n)}=poly(n)-size "catalytic" tape that is initialized with an arbitrary string and must be restored to that exact initial content at the end of the computation. The machine must accept/reject correctly for every possible initial content of the catalytic tape. With an oracle D, CL^D is defined analogously, allowing oracle queries to D, and EXP^D is the class of languages decidable in deterministic time 2^{poly(n)} with oracle access to D.

Problem: Does there exist an oracle D such that CL^D = EXP^D?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Cook et al., October 2025, "The Structure of In-Place Space-Bounded Computation") constructs an oracle O for which CL^O = EXP^O, thereby showing that any proof of CL ⊆ P must use non-relativizing techniques. This appears to resolve the problem affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: The Structure of In-Place Space-Bounded Computation
status_evidence.snippet: There is an oracle O for which CL^O = EXP^O, so any proof of CL ⊆ P must be non-relativizing.
status_evidence.claim: An oracle O with CL^O = EXP^O has been constructed.
